annotations.title: Google Ads conversion goals (what smart bidding optimises for)

description: Which conversion goals Google Ads smart bidding optimises toward, the usual cause of "it optimises for the wrong thing". With no goals it reads: the account goals, or with campaignId that campaign's goals and whether it follows the account. goals:[{category (PURCHASE, SIGNUP, SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM, PAGE_VIEW...), origin (default WEBSITE), biddable}] sets them account-wide, or for one campaign with campaignId (it then stops following account changes). useAccountGoals:true puts a campaign back on the account goals. A goal exists only where a conversion action of that category exists. Changing goals of LIVE campaigns needs confirm:true after the user approves. Read back from Google.

confirm.description: true only after the user approved a change to a LIVE campaign or a delete

customerId.description: omit to use the selected default account

goals.description: conversion goals to set, as a list of {category, origin, biddable}; omit to read the current goals

biddable.description: true = smart bidding optimises for this goal

category.description: goal category, e.g. PURCHASE, SIGNUP, SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM or PAGE_VIEW

origin.description: where the conversion happens, e.g. WEBSITE; default WEBSITE

loginCustomerId.description: manager id if operating through an MCC

useAccountGoals.description: put the campaign back on the account goals

name: set_google_ads_conversion_goals
